web_evidence.title: BLOW FLY

web_evidence.title: Cornwell Abandons Forensics and Scarpetta in ‘At Risk’

search_log: Searched for "Patricia Cornwell Blow Fly novel point of view third person review" and "Blow Fly Patricia Cornwell first person third person narration"; opened the Guardian/Observer, Kirkus, and Harvard Crimson discussions.
Searched for "Patricia Cornwell Blow Fly excerpt chapter 1" and opened both pages of BookBrowse's permission-authorized Chapter 1 excerpt.

Searched for "Blow Fly Patricia Cornwell omniscient multiple viewpoints narrator" and for epistolary, diary, frame-narrative, and alternating-person descriptions; results consistently described multiple third-person focal viewpoints, not alternating grammatical persons.

Searched the author's site, Penguin Random House, and Google Books; their accessible pages supplied synopsis or catalog material rather than additional diagnostic prose, so they were not used as person evidence.
person_note: The diagnostic Goodreads passages externally narrate Benton, another character's convictions, and Jean-Baptiste, while the many first- and second-person forms occur only in aphorisms or dialogue. The authorized opening independently maintains third-person narration, and whole-book sources explicitly identify an omniscient third-person structure with several character viewpoints. Those viewpoint changes remain within third person and therefore do not warrant ALTERNATING. The opening excerpt alone has limited scope, but the whole-book structural accounts and interior quote evidence remove the material uncertainty.
